title: Workflows, agents, and who owns the control flow

items.stem: In the usual distinction between a workflow and an agent, which difference decides which one a system is?

options.text: How many different tools the system can call during one request
How large the model is that writes each of the answers
Whether the code or the model decides the next step
Whether the system keeps results from earlier conversations

items.stem: In your makerspace assistant, the program always does the same two things for a manual question: it first calls search_manuals with the student's question, then it gives the top passages to the model, which writes the answer. How is this best described?

options.text: A workflow: the program fixes the order and the model only writes text
An agent: the system calls a tool and the model reads the result
An agent: the model produces the final answer that the student sees
Neither: a workflow cannot include any call to a language model

items.stem: Your sponsor's model budget is small. Which of these tasks is the best candidate for a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Fixing a failing script in a code repository nobody has opened before
Planning a student's project and deciding which machines it will need
Answering whatever questions students think of about the makerspace
Booking a slot: check the calendar, reserve it, send a confirmation

items.stem: For a booking request, a fixed workflow always makes exactly 2 model calls. An agent doing the same job averages 5 model calls. Assume every model call costs $0.004. For 200 booking requests in one week, how much more does the agent cost than the workflow, in dollars?
In one sentence, what property of a task makes an agent a better choice than a fixed workflow?

Your assistant first asks the model to label each student message as either "manual question" or "booking request". The program then runs one of two step sequences that your team wrote in advance. Who owns the control flow?

options.text: The model, because its label decides which path the program takes
The program: your team wrote both paths and the model only picks one
Nobody, because the path changes from one student message to the next
The student, because the message they type decides which path is run
